body: Phantasy Star Nova is tri-Ace's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 November 2014. It places a customisable character inside a mission-driven adventure with a strong single-player story and encounters against enormous creatures. Completing assignments advances the narrative and expands the possibilities for the developing party. The game shares elements with Phantasy Star Online 2 while changing familiar powers through its own story circumstances. Motoi Sakuraba's score accompanies a portable entry that brings tri-Ace's action role-playing experience into Sega's established science-fiction universe.

Different classes offer close combat, ranged weapons or techniques, while the new Pile weapon fires anchors that can create weak points on enemies. That gives the player a way to change the target rather than merely select an existing vulnerable spot. Weapons are crafted from gathered materials instead of obtained as direct item drops, connecting exploration and combat to preparation. The choice of class determines which tools can be used effectively. A successful mission therefore contributes both to immediate story progress and to the equipment that will make a later giant opponent more manageable.

The character's name and appearance can be customised using a creation system related to Phantasy Star Online 2. Local ad-hoc cooperation lets up to four Vita players participate together, even as the main story remains central to the design. Sega announced the project in 2013, and a Chinese-language Asian edition followed in 2015. Nova gives the portable series a distinct production identity through tri-Ace and Sakuraba. Its most characteristic encounters connect scale and preparation, asking a comparatively small character to create a useful opening in a creature that occupies much of the battlefield.
